messages:
anya: hey — during the nightly load run the new quantized runner started applying a hard backpressure at ~1.2k tokens/s per shard, even though targets are 2.5k. results show throughput collapse and cost-per-token spikes. anyone seen this pattern?
jun-ho: saw a blip earlier, thought it was infra noise. do you have the runner logs?
anya: pasted main fragment below: 
```
2026-01-29T04:12:07Z runner[pid=8421] INFO  batcher: scheduling 64 reqs, shard=0
2026-01-29T04:12:07Z runner[pid=8421] WARN  backpressure: queue_length=512 threshold=256 apply=true
2026-01-29T04:12:07Z runner[pid=8421] INFO  kernel: selected int8-path quant_profile=fast32
2026-01-29T04:12:07Z runner[pid=8421] ERROR kvcache: prefetch stall detected, inflight=8
2026-01-29T04:12:08Z runner[pid=8421] INFO  backpressure: applied delay=120ms
```
anya: that 120ms delay multiplied across micro-batches killed tail latency and effective throughput.
mike_g: hmm kvcache prefetch stall + backpressure. could be our new prefetch window interacting with continuous batching. what's the repo sha?
anya: sha: a3f4b9c — the change was reducing prefetch concurrency from 16 -> 8 and adding an adaptive-delay in backpressure that scales with queue length.
olivia: can you share the small repro? even a limited-scope runner config would help (we can run locally).
anya: quick config snip: 
```
batch_size: adaptive
max_inflight_prefetch: 8
batcher.max_queue: 1024
backpressure.policy: queue-proportional
backpressure.base_ms: 30
backpressure.scale_per_256: 90
```
anya: the policy math: delay = base_ms + floor(queue/256)*scale_per_256. so at queue 512 -> 30 + 2*90 = 210ms, but logs show 120ms (maybe scaled by shard?).
jun-ho: that formula looks aggressive for high-concurrency evals. We normally cap delay at ~50ms for hosted profiles to avoid SLO blowouts. Did the change forget the global cap?
anya: good call — I don't see a cap in the diff. we should also check that queue metric is global versus per-batcher. if it's per-shard we can miscompute.
ci-bot: test-run queued: runner-loadtest/2026-01-29-04:10 (id 8792) started
mike_g: if prefetch inflight stalls, lowering prefetch concurrency helps avoid memory pressure but also increases misses which triggers more KV reads and stalls — a sweet spot exists. we need an automated sweep that records cost/token vs latency with the adaptive backpressure toggled.
olivia: i'll add a short CI job: 4 runs per config (prefetch=4,8,12,16) x backpressure=(on,off) with 30s ramp and 2 minute steady-state. should fit into perf tier.
anya: thanks. one more oddity — the kernel chosen was int8-path/fast32. maybe that path increases per-token variance so batcher sees more jitter and overreacts. can we force-only fp16 to see if behavior changes?
jun-ho: yes force path by env: REDWOOD_FORCE_FP16=1 for the worker. also capture per-batch timing histogram, not just avg.
mike_g: also add cost-per-token calculation: (gpu_seconds * gpu_price) / tokens_generated. Want to see cost regressions if backpressure increases wall-time.
anya: planning to run the matrix now. starting with forcing fp16 + prefetch 8 + backpressure disabled to get baseline. will post results in this thread.
ci-bot: test-run completed: runner-loadtest/2026-01-29-04:22 (id 8792) status=FAIL flakiness=high
anya: first quick result: disabling backpressure removed the 120ms delays and throughput recovered to ~2.6k tokens/s. cost/token dropped by ~18%. but tail P95 latency increased slightly.
jun-ho: that aligns with backpressure tradeoff — it trades lower tail spikes for steady throughput. we need smarter policy: use EWMA of queue length or per-batch timeouts instead of raw queue bins.
mike_g: propose: compute short-window EWMA of batch latency; trigger micro-delay only when EWMA > latency_target and also when kvcache-stalls > threshold. avoids punting on transient queue spikes.
anya: agreed. i'll PR a prototype: add ewma_alpha=0.2, kv_stall_thresh=4, and a global cap 60ms. will run full sweep (prefetch 4/8/12/16, force_fp16 on/off) and record cost/latency histograms.
olivia: also add exporter metrics: backpressure.applied_ms, ewma_latency_ms, kvcache.stall_count. dashboards should show applied_ms vs tokens/s.
anya: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/2123 — running CI matrix now. will update with consolidated numbers and dashboard links. :thumbsup:
